cards.explanation: The reason is that their hearts plan violence. The teacher says, “…for their hearts devise violence, and their lips declare trouble.” So it's what they plan inside and what comes out of their mouths. Wishing for their company is like asking to ride along with the guy who keeps setting off the smoke alarm on purpose. The teacher says skip it, friends. (Proverbs 24:1–2)

The rooms are filled with every precious and beautiful treasure. Through knowledge the rooms are filled with “…every precious and beautiful treasure.” Notice he says every one, not just a few. A house built wisely ends up with treasures in all its rooms, and it beats a house full of loose crumbs and good intentions. (Proverbs 24:3–4)

The word is counselors. The teacher says, “Only with sound guidance should you wage war, and victory lies in a multitude of counselors.” One voice can miss something, so he points to many. Even a stamper like me asks around before moving the big oven. It's hard to out-guess a whole room of good advice, friends. (Proverbs 24:6)

The answer is False. The teacher says, “Wisdom is too high for a fool; he does not open his mouth in the meeting place.” So at that meeting, the fool isn't the one talking. Wisdom is out of his reach, so he stays quiet, friends. (Proverbs 24:7)

People see a mocker as detestable. The teacher says, “…a mocker is detestable to men.” Detestable is a strong word, and he picks it on purpose. A mocker might think he's the life of the party, but the verse says that's not how people see him. Laughing with folks is a gift, friends, and laughing at them is a different thing. (Proverbs 24:9)

The answer is True. The teacher says, “If you faint in the day of distress, how small is your strength!” He's saying hard days show how much strength you really have. I think we all find out on a day like that what we're made of. Thankfully, he's already told us that wisdom makes a person strong (Proverbs 24:5). (Proverbs 24:10)

The answer is the One who guards your life. The teacher imagines someone saying they didn't know about this, and then he asks, “Does not the One who guards your life know?” He also asks whether He who weighs hearts considers it. So the question points to the One who guards your life. Nobody gets to say they didn't know, friends. (Proverbs 24:11–12)

The word is deeds. The teacher asks, “Will He not repay a man according to his deeds?” It's the last of three questions in a row, and he leaves them hanging. Each one is a nudge that what we do matters. I think the questions land harder than a lecture would, friends. (Proverbs 24:12)

The word is wisdom. After the honey, the teacher says, “Know therefore that wisdom is sweet to your soul.” He's saying wisdom is good for you the way honey is good to your taste. The sweetness just goes deeper, down to the soul. Good thing the teacher doesn't make us pick between them, friends. (Proverbs 24:13–14)

The answer is True. He says, “If you find it, there is a future for you, and your hope will never be cut off.” That's a promise worth holding onto, friends. Compare it with the evil man, who has no future (Proverbs 24:20). Wisdom leaves your hope in one piece. (Proverbs 24:14)

The righteous man still gets up. “For though a righteous man may fall seven times, he still gets up…” The verse doesn't say he never falls. It says he gets back up after each one. I know a thing or two about tipping over, and this verse gives me hope, friends. (Proverbs 24:16)

The word is stumble. The verse says, “but the wicked stumble in bad times.” Right before it, the teacher says a righteous man may fall seven times and still gets up. The verse puts those two pictures side by side, friends. (Proverbs 24:16)

The LORD would turn His wrath away from your enemy. The verse says, “…or the LORD will see and disapprove, and turn His wrath away from him.” The teacher says the LORD sees it, and He disapproves of the gloating. So a victory dance can backfire. I'd rather keep my feet still and my heart quiet, friends. (Proverbs 24:17–18)

The two words are future and extinguished. The teacher says, “For the evil man has no future…” It's the reason not to envy him. A big, flashy life that goes nowhere isn't worth wanting. Then he says, “the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.” A lamp that goes out leaves a room dark, and that's a picture of the end of the wicked. It's a cold picture, friends, which is why envying them makes no sense. (Proverbs 24:19–20)

The answer is the rebellious. “My son, fear the LORD and the king, and do not associate with the rebellious.” The teacher puts those together in one breath. I think he's saying who you hang around with shapes where you end up. So choose your crowd the way you choose your dough, friends, carefully. (Proverbs 24:21)

The answer is False. The teacher says, “For they will bring sudden destruction.” Then he asks, “Who knows what ruin they can bring?” I'd rather be around people who bring cookies, friends. (Proverbs 24:22)
